So, again, they're trying to reopen their case without asking for the Chamber to reopen their case and to adduce positive evidence in relation to the indictment which I believe, again, is wholly improper under the Rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I can respond. I did not say or certainly did not intend to say that this particular document is part of our indictment. What I meant to say is that Prijedor and the cleansing of non-Serbs from Prijedor is a part of our indictment and the cleansing of non-Serbs from Prijedor in September and October is part of our indictment which runs until the 30th of November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Chamber will MFI the document and we will deal with it later. Madam.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31619 receives number P6925, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: MFI'd, marked for identification. While we are at this stage, Mr. Jeremy, you asked that P3094 have uploaded translations, to substitute that. Shall we do that now? Madam Registrar, document P0046440/A/ET to replace the current translation of P3094. Is that correct? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. That concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jeremy. Any re-examination, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There is, Your Honours. I see that we are about seven minutes beyond the time for a break, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you for that help. We will take a break at this time and come back in 20 minutes time again, Mr. Corokalo. You may follow the usher. We take a break and we will come back at 20 minutes past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think we have to wait for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now I can say "Mr. Ivetic."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to go back to your testimony in relation to the fighting and the operation to disarm the Mahala neighbourhood. First of all, I'd like to ask you: You mentioned in the cross-examination a Captain Radak who came with the unit that actually within into Mahala. Can you tell us what entity or organisation did Captain Radak and his unit belong to?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Radak was commander of the 4th Battalion at that stage, the preparation stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your microphone was not activated, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 4th Battalion of which army?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can call up in e-court Exhibit P2889.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: While we wait for the same, I can introduce that document that was used with you in cross-examination. That is, a 15 June 1992 report of the Ministry of the Interior, that is the public security station, the police. Mr. Jeremy focused on the third paragraph of the document. I would like to first focus on the second paragraph, which reads as follows: "The action of peaceful disarming and surrendering of weapons was carried out in the period between 10 May and 25 May 1992. During that period, the Muslim and Croatian population handed over only hunting weapons and other legally owned weapons, but illegally obtained military weapons were not surrendered, and were concealed (buried) on instructions from above." I'd like to ask you, sir, is this paragraph consistent with the information, operative and security information, that was available to you prior to the 4th Battalion going in to the Mahala neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can look at the fourth paragraph in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It talks about after the action, the military action against the Mahala, and says: "After these combat actions, military police and civilian police arrested and brought in members of Muslim paramilitary formations, who were processed to obtain information about weapons available to their membership. On the basis of data gathered so far, it was determined that the Muslim population had been relatively well armed, predominantly with Infantry weapons and mines and explosives. This was followed by an action of seizing these weapons from persons who were determined during the investigation process to have weapons in their possession. The action was jointly carried out by military police and civilian police. It is still going on, and it can be said that it has only just started."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, just -- I don't want to interrupt Mr. Ivetic, but I'll just make an interjection before he asks his question. Mr. Ivetic has said that paragraph 4 talks about the military action against Mahala, and just so the record is clear, it's actually referring to military action -- paragraph 3 is referring to military action is Mahala, Vrhpolje, and Hrustovo, and paragraph 4 is making a reference to those military actions. So just so that is clear for all of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I agree and I think I actually said that it was talking about after the action because that indeed is the paragraph. And I think at line 21 of page 49, I did say "after the action," so I think I correctly identified that paragraph as talking about after the actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yeah. Just to be clear, you said: "Paragraph 4 talks about after the action, the military action against the Mahala." So I just want to make it clear that we're talking about Mahala, Hrustovo, and Vrhpolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, the paragraph I have just read out to you, is that consistent with the information that was reported back to you of how weapons were uncovered or discovered?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's absolutely consistent. I have to stress that a number of people whom we didn't find there were from Mahala, Otoke, Muhici, and other Muslim inhabitants. They were in the armed formation. From Mahala specifically is Fera.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And from the bottom of the page we see that there is a table enclosed of quantities of weapons, although it says that "the army data is not too precise because they don't have precise data."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the first page that Mr. Jeremy just directed us to indicated that 2.000 individuals, it says "civilians," were taken in or captured during this operation. The resulting weapons from those 2.000 civilians from the three villages by my count is approximately 700 weapons. Now I know that you said that you did not know about quantities of weapons, but looking at the types of weapons that are listed here, is that consistent with the information that you were receiving subsequent to the operation as to the type of weapons that were recovered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, just again so the record is clear, where we see the reference in this document to 2.000 individuals, that is in relation to Mahala. It's not in relation to the three villages that Mr. Ivetic just referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct. It's 2.000 and then 800 men. In the next -- the next two lines down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. Except that what Mr. Jeremy is saying is that these weapons do not relate to Mahala but they relate to all three areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I think I said that they relate to all three areas in my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is this, sir, consistent in terms of the type of weaponry that was recovered and handed over both to the SJB and to the army as a result of these operations?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of structure, yes, but numerically I can't answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I appreciate that. Thank you, sir. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, just a clarification. I think it's not working at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can hear you, Your Honour. So it is working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'll try this one. You can hear me directly, I think. You said the two -- you were referring to all the three villages, but in your question you made a different connection, that the witness indicate -- no, the document indicated that 2.000 individuals, it says "civilians," were taken or captured during this operation. And only in the -- with which you said then: "2.000 villages from the three villages." I don't have the first page on my screen at the moment, but the 2.000 captured civilians were only from one village, Mahala; is that correct? Perhaps you can see the first --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: From the document that's what it says, but the weapons are from all three villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, but you said the 2.000 civilians from the three villages and that caused the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Ah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- complication, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think you're right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now -- that worked a little too well, the microphone. Now in terms of the 800 individuals that are listed on the first page --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can go pack to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- that were broken up and militarily defeated in Vrhpolje and Hrustovo, how did those individuals relate to the armed group in Golaja that you talk about in paragraphs 13 and 14 of your statement, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know about that linking up. I did not have such information. I don't know how they did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can have P6924 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You will see, I think, this is another document that Mr. Jeremy used with you in cross-examination. In fact, he tendered it during cross-examination. And you were asked to comment about item number 1. I would like to look at item number 2 with you, where it lists a total of four military conscripts who have been detained on reasonable grounds of suspicion of plundering several houses in Skender Vakuf and mistreating the civilian population. Is this behaviour of the authorities, detaining military conscripts for these actions, consistent with your knowledge of the situation that prevailed within your brigade of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wherever it was possible to establish something like that, I suppose that was the procedure. I don't know about the cases where we were not sure. But when we knew about cases like that, then we did it that way. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could then also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I just put an additional question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Here in the document we can see the suspicion of plundering several houses in Skender Vakuf and mistreating the civilian population. Do you know anything about these events of plundering and mistreating the civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not have any occasion to find out. It's pretty far away from me, but I know by the names of these people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you know which kind of civilian population this is referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose that it was the Muslim population inhabiting that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But you don't know for a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to P3095 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is a document that was shown to you in relation to the discussion about Arkan that you had with Prosecution counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can turn to page 2 of the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in the last sentence of the first paragraph, it says: "Since so far these formations have not taken part in combat activities and are not a part of any formation unit and have not reported to any command from the level of Battalion to the VRS GS to be given an assignment, obviously they are paramilitary formations acting independently of the VRS." Is this consistent with the view of how Arkan's men were viewed by yourself and other officers in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what were the standing orders or the position taken by the VRS since the beginning of the war in relation to paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The position was that the paramilitaries should be either integrated or disarmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean integrated into the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now in regards to the description of Mr. Raznjatovic's appearance -- activities, it says here: "Raznjatovic's appearances at the command posts in the ZO of some units have so far had as their purpose bullying, mistreatment, and physical abuse of officers, kidnapping and taking away members of units, disarming parts of units for the purpose of confiscating material and technical equipment, MTS, and combat hardware, unauthorised opening of gun-fire on members of the VRS, tearing up official and identification documents of VRS members." In relation to the conduct of Arkan's men towards the VRS, are the things listed in this document consistent with what you either saw or heard from others that was happening in Sanski Most in 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't see it because I was relocated. But I heard that such things happened, people were stripped of rank, slapped, beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And approximately how long did you remain in Sanski Most before having to flee Sanski Most after this time-period?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beginning with the 21st -- the 21st September when I came back from the front line from Jasenica and Benakovac until the 10th October when I fled. But my whole involvement was in touring Bosanski Novi to see if any of our people would get out and to find those 98 missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, for those that may not know, why did you have to flee Sanski Most on or about the 10th of October, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the reason is well known. On the 10th of October, from 8.00 in the morning, because we were invited in a meeting, all of us who meant something in Sanski Most, from business leaders, police officers, et cetera, were invited at a meeting at Rasula's office. The shelling began. Shells were falling around the secondary school centre, and it began in the morning and increased in intensity until the afternoon, by which time the people from that area, from Tomina and the left bank of the river, had clogged all the passages across the river, all the bridges. The so-called machine bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Who was shelling?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as we were able to tell, those were rapid action forces. They were acting so destructively that it must have been them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say "rapid reaction forces," of what entity did they belong? What army or entity?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was part of NATO. The Muslim forces were not capable of anything like that. Until the fall of Sanski Most. After the fall of Sanski Most, the Muslims joined in.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now my last topic I'd like to discuss with you are the events at the bridge at Vrhpolje. The first thing I want to ask you is Mr. Jeremy intimated to you that members of the VRS may have been involved in that killing that occurred in May of 1992. I'd like to ask you about something that the survivor of that incident said in court on transcript page 2189. He described the unit as follows: "That unit which came to our village on the 25th of May, 1992 was commanded by a commander with long black hair tied in a ponytail. He wore round dark glasses." And then further on, it is said: "He wore black leather gloves which he never took off." Later, the same individual said: "The unit was commanded by the Chetnik whom I previously described as having a long ponytail." Sir, based upon that description of the perpetrators of that incident, do they sound like the appearance of VRS personnel from your brigade?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the description, long hair, hip crowd. Conditionally speaking, we had no such men. At least I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And what type of information did you hear about this incident as to what actually happened? What caused this to happen, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I didn't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, certainly not. I said I don't know. I don't know what could have happened, what could have been the cause.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, again on behalf of General Mladic and the rest of the Defence team, I thank you for answering our questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that completes my redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do have one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: One question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, you were asked in re-examination about Arkan and you were asked about your own departure from Sanski Most in 1995. Now, we looked at a newspaper article at the end of your cross-examination from Vreme International that I quoted from, and in that article, it referred to the departure of 5.000 people from Prijedor. And I -- I wanted to know what information -- I want to know if you are aware that in 1995, in October 1995, 5.000 non-Serbs left Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that has been asked and answered in cross, and it certainly does not arise out of my redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was it asked in cross? Where was it asked?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Give me a moment, Your Honours. I believe the witness said -- I believe he indicated that he did not have any knowledge of Prijedor. That was at -- I have that once at transcript page 42, line 6. There is a discussion of --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: That's about Arkan's crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Around 5.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then at -- at page 47, lines 1 through 5, Mr. Jeremy introduced the idea of cleansing of non-Serbs from Prijedor from October of 1995, and he did not ask the witness a question of it. So I think that, in that sense, he had the opportunity. He was not -- it's not an issue I raised again in redirect. They can't have a second bite at the apple.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Ivetic, you asked the witness - this can be found at page 56, the last three lines, and the answer then follows on page 57 - about the reasons why -- for fleeing Sanski Most in October 1995. I just state.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct. And the question that Mr. Jeremy is asking is related to Prijedor, not to Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Ivetic has gone back into this question of Arkan in this region in 1995. He's gone into the issue of persons leaving these areas in October 1995. My question is squarely within the remit of that sphere, and I would submit that it's perfectly appropriate for me to ask this witness this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may ask the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So, sir, very simply you are aware, are you not, that in October 1995 5.000 non-Serbs left Prijedor as described in the article that I showed to you during cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO COROKALO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I absolutely had no knowledge and I don't know how I could have had it. Now, I had to fight for my own life. On the 10th of October, I left Sanski Most at 7.30 at night. I don't know where -- I didn't know where my family was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I stop you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So how could I have known? I couldn't even get the papers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have answered the question. You don't have to tell us about your personal situation. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions. Although I would submit that, in respect to the tendering of this document that's been MFI'd, that's a further ground for tendering of that document in that it relates to the credibility of this witness, that he didn't know about the departure of 5.000 persons from his neighbouring municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We've heard you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, for the record, then, could we also have the Prosecution stipulate that Vreme is published in Serbia, not in Bosnia? Can we get that stipulation, that Vreme is published and distributed in Serbia, not in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's something that I won't do right now and I'll need to verify that, but my understanding is that it is a Serbian publication. Where it's published, I'm not clear. Although I do understand that Vreme International is a publication that is published outside of Serbia and not simply within Serbia, and I would note that this article comes from Vreme International. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The parties will come back to the Chamber about that point, at which time I guess the Chamber will decide on the admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Judge, any questions to the witness? Mr. Corokalo, that brings us to the conclusion of your testimony in this court. You are now free to go home. Thank you very much for coming all the way to come and testify, and may you please travel back home safely. Mr. Ivetic, does the Defence have a next witness ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We do, Your Honours. My colleague, Mr. Stojanovic, will be handling the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I ask if we are fetching the witness, to verify?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Sarenac, I suppose. Before you make -- give your evidence, the Rules require that you make a declaration to tell the whole -- the truth, and the declaration has been given to you. Will you please read out the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You will first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic and he's to your left. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: According to our customary procedure here, would you please tell us your full name.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: I am Rajko Sarenac, and I am a member of the Serbian ethnicity from Bosnia and Herzegovina. I participated in the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I was a member of the Republika Srpska Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sarenac, at one point in time did you provide -- did you make a statement to the Defence of General Mladic in writing?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes. And I signed that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we have 65 ter 1D01736 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sarenac, could you please take a look at the screen. Can you tell us whether what we see on this cover page of this statement, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sarenac, please, wait a minute. Is this signature and the date that appears on this document, is this your signature and did you put in that date?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to -- I would like you to look at paragraph 20 of this statement. Mr. Sarenac, did you, during the preparation for your appearance before the Court, did you point out that in the penultimate line in the English version and then the last line in the B/C/S version, the word Sulic, last name, was mistyped? It should be Zulic, Z?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes, it should be Zulic with a Z.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With this typographical correction and after having made the solemn declaration before this Court, would you provide the same answers and would those answers be the full truth about the events that you are testifying about?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender document 65 ter 1D01736 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No objection. 1D01736 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1736 receives number D786, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, the name "Zulic" in both versions is written with a Z. I really don't understand what the correction would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in B/C/S it is a Zu, Zulic, not Z, Zulic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can assist, it's the accent mark that should not be on the Z. So it's the Z but it's the accent mark that is the difference between two letters in the Serbo-Croatian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps it's just the way I pronounced it that it didn't come across clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That is clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would also like to tender an associated exhibit which relates to paragraph 17 of the statement. And under 65 ter, that bears the number 1D05027.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weber. 1D05027 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D5027 receives number D787, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, I would like to read the witness -- the resume or the short statement of this witness, the summary statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may do so. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Colonel Rajko Sarenac held a number of jobs of high responsibility, beginning with a job at the Operations Group Kupres followed by his post as assistant commander for moral, religious, and legal affairs in a number of VRS units at first within the 2nd Krajina Corps, then within the Guards Brigade, attached to the Main Staff of the VRS, and then as chief of armoured and mechanised units, and a trainer at the training centre in Bileca and military school centre Rajko Balac in Banja Luka. With his unit, he was in a number of theatres of war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, including the theatres in Bratunac, Srebrenica, Gorazde, Jahorina, Trnovo, Nisic plateau, and the general area around Vares. He speaks about his experiences that he went through at those theatres. He witnessed General Mladic's treatment of a captured member of the BH police forces in Trnovo in July 1993, and he's aware of the position of the Main Staff of the VRS on the reception and pull-out of the Croatian population from the Vares general area. He says that several thousand people, men, women, old men, and children were evacuated from there. They were sent towards Sarajevo and Kiseljak via the territory under VRS control, or across VRS territory. He also testifies that after the evacuation of the Croatian population from Vares, an HVO unit was established, the Croatian Defence Council, which together with VRS units secured positions at the Nisic plateau. The witness met General Mladic on several occasions on the basis of which he saw that his family and military background, his integrity and perseverance, stand in great contrast with the crimes of genocide that he is charged with. After the war, the witness worked in the commission for the gathering of documents on crimes against the Serbs where he had occasion to meet on several occasions with representatives of The Hague Tribunal that related to the exchange or, rather, hand-over of documents relevant to the job that the witness performed at that time. Your Honours, this is the summary statement of this witness, and I would now like to ask him several questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you do that, you said that related to the exchange or, rather, hand-over of documents relevant to the job that the witness performed at that time. Hand-over of these documents by who to who and what documents are these?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, paragraph 30 of the witness statement deals with that. The witness handed over documents that had been gathered and that related to a case before this court. And as a representative of that commission attached to the VRS, he actually had these documents in his possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I see the time. I have about -- I need about ten more minutes, so perhaps this would be the right moment to take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can't use the next five and use the ten later when you come back?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sarenac, could you please take a look at the following document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, for the record, I'll say that now this is document D786.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 20 of your statement, where you say that you remember the moment when, together with a complement of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps units, you entered Trnovo, and at the time the Main Staff commander of the VRS was at the head of it. And then you talk about the commander of the police station in Trnovo. And based on what it says here, could you please tell us, briefly, your observations of the situation, your direct observations of the situation, that you mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. On that day, which was the 11th of July, 1993 in the afternoon, when the Guards Brigade units entered, and I was with the Guards Brigade units, at that same time, the commander of the Main Staff, General Mladic, entered Trnovo. When we entered Trnovo and came to the centre, all of a sudden from the direction of Treskavica hotel, a shot -- or several shots could be heard, but that's not really relevant, whether it was one or more, but the security and members of the army at that moment headed for the hotel, and General Mladic headed there, too. Immediately following that, perhaps a few minutes later, a vehicle came towards us, a police vehicle. When this vehicle was stopped by one of our members and when his ID was checked, the man said who he was and why he was there and where he was headed. He provided a brief statement. He said that he was on the way to his home, allegedly, to take his sports shoes. Soon thereafter, General Mladic arrived. He saw immediately what the situation was. He exchanged a few words with this person mentioned here, Zulic, and then he pulled the man aside, talked to him, and realised that he was the person who was -- thanks to whom, in fact, General Mladic's uncle and aunt were saved because he intervened, and he said that he was the person most responsible, most credited for it. After this, after this conversation with General Mladic, General Mladic said that if that was true, everything will be all right. It would probably have been all right anyway. But because he said that this was true, that he was credited for saving these people, and unfortunately not many men were saved, he then turned to a colonel and said to him, "Lazo, this man, no harm should come to this man. Provide security and when I return we will take him over and he will be exchanged." That's how it happened in the end, that was the outcome. And I learned, although I didn't see it myself, that later on General Mladic arranged for the said Zulic and the other two people that he had allegedly saved meet on Mount Jahorina at the hotel on which occasion this person provided his statement that was then shown on Serbian television. That's all on my part. If you have some additional questions, I can answer them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sarenac. I will have a few more questions but that will come after the break.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, we will take a break. And, Mr. Sarenac, we will take a break for 20 minutes. Will you please follow the usher and we will see you in 20 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We take a break and will resume at 20 to 2.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the witness please be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we please bring up in e-court D786. Let me just repeat for the record, D786. And let us focus on paragraph 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sarenac, in paragraph 24, you talk about your unit's stay on the plateau, and you say that with a part of the units of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps and the Drina Corps, you took control of the Nisici-Brgule-Vares road with the aim of receiving and evacuating the Croat population from the general area of Vares pursuant to the orders of the Main Staff of the VRS, and you mention the total number of people who got out at that time. Do you have any more detailed information as to how and in which way these Croat expellees left for Kiseljak and Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Can I start? May I start answering?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: The Croat populous that lived around Vares was under threat from the Muslim forces. They probably decided on their own to try to get out of that dangerous area around Vares. The only way out was the road leading towards the territory controlled by the VRS, and that's the road Vares-Brgule-Nisici and onto Kiseljak and Sarajevo. The Main Staff of the VRS, after receiving this information, issued an order to its units, including the 1st Guards Brigade, that this road should be unblocked and that it should be made possible to receive and allow the Croat population to evacuate. Among those civilians, there were also members of the HVO of Vares. After they got out, I received a report that General Mladic showed up on one section of the road in order to reassure those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm just standing to express my concern. The Chamber has received evidence related to the events in Vares. I was just wondering if in this discussion we could have a little time context. There is a reference to an order from the VRS Main Staff and then a following report. If -- when we're discussing this, if we could break it down a little bit just so we could have some temporal understanding of how it's related to the other evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You heard, Mr. Sarenac. I am directing you again to paragraph 24. It says: "In December 1993, I was sent to the Nisici plateau," but the Prosecutor is asking was this happening in December 1993 or after the new year in 1994? Could you give us a more precise time-frame?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: That's the end of 1993. Let me just add that after the Croat population pulled out, a unit was formed led by one of their commanders who continued to operate in co-ordination with our forces to secure positions facing Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sarenac, for your answers. That was all for the moment. Now you will be examined by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just before beginning with the examination. Just so I understand clearly, is it then that -- is it the Defence's position that all these things happened from December 1993 onward, according to this witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you asking the Defence or do you want to ask that from the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: To me, it's still not clear from the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it -- wouldn't you be able to clarify it with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I can ask the first question if you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I suggest you ask the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks, Judge. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Sarenac, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Weber. Mr. Weber represents the Prosecution in this case, and you will see him to your right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Sarenac.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just want to very quickly pick up where the questioning just left off. Do I understand correctly that your evidence related to the departure of the Croat population and members of the HVO relates to events that occurred from December 1993 and thereafter?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Could you be more specific? What occurred in December 1993? I've already said that the Croat population pulled out from Vares towards the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It is very simple. Everything you described happened from December 1993 and thereafter, today? I'm not going to spend a lot time with you on this. I'm just asking you to confirm it. It appears that that's what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Not from December. Towards the end of 1993. Not only December necessarily. It could have been in November, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: I did not mention a date, a particular day. Towards the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right. That's less clear but I understand that that's what you know. I'm going to move on and talk about your statement quickly and some information that's in it before we finish at the end of today. In paragraphs 4, 6, and 7 of your statement, you discuss the liberation of Kupres in April 1992. Is it correct that Kupres is a municipality in western Bosnia and Herzegovina bordering the Bosnian Krajina, which is to the north?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes. It's in the territory of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the western part of it, Kupres itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The JNA 9th Corps participated in the liberation of Kupres; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: General Mladic was present in the area of Kupres during these operations?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was present. At the time when I came, he wasn't there or during the liberation. He visited later. But I cannot tell you which date. It was in the beginning of April. I know he came, I was at negotiations with Croats then in Pakovo Selo. We were negotiating about a possible exchange of our captives.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, the Chamber has received evidence through General Mladic's notebooks that he attended a meeting in Sipovo, which is just to the north of Kupres, on the 4th of April, 1992. Is this the period in which you became aware that General Mladic was in Bosnia around this time, near Kupres?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: General Mladic was at that time commander of the Knin Corps, and he had received orders from the General Staff of the SFRY that he should move with his units to liberate Kupres from paramilitary Croat forces. There was no JNA presence at Kupres. It was simply that the entire population was attacked by Croat military and paramilitary forces. They captured Kupres --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, we are going to go through the operations. If you can listen carefully to my questions, we'll actually go very quickly. In paragraph 6 of your statement, you indicate that General Mladic telephoned you following the liberation of Kupres. Where were you when he called you?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Right. I was in the operations centre of the operative group at Kupres. I was the officer on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where was General Mladic calling from?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: I suppose from his command post in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. What -- do you recall the approximate date of this call?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: 8 or 9 April. I don't remember the exact date. But it was in the beginning of April after the fighting had stopped. He called me, and I can quote approximately what he said --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, sir, sir, sir, if we could go with my questions here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P3090 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, sir, I'd like to discuss with you before we end today the activities of the JNA 9th Corps immediately before and during the operations in Kupres. Before you will be a 5 April 1992 JNA 9th Corps regular combat report from General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Toward the end of item 4 --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Which is at the bottom of the page in the B/C/S, if we could please have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- General Mladic refers to a 9th Corps request and 2nd Military District order and states: "We ask that the units in the Kupres region be given logistical support."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we now please have page 2 of the B/C/S original.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: General Mladic then articulates his decisions, the first one is: "To follow the activities of the part of mobilised men in the Kupres region and to maintain and heighten the level of combat readiness of the mobilised men." Is it correct, sir, that General Mladic and the 9th Corps were involved in mobilising and providing logistical support to men in the area of Kupres at the outset of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: General Mladic was the commander, but with his orders he made his subordinates responsible for doing this. Some of the units, so parts of the units of the Knin Corps, were involved in combat now and he was issuing combat assignments. I don't see what's controversial here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm not looking to actually -- sir, I'm just going through the information with you. We also see in this document that General Mladic orders to continue with the mobilisation forming, equipping, and arming of the mobilised units in Bosansko Grahovo and Bosanski Petrovac. Those were also formations that were to the -- in Bosnia to the west of Kupres, correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: East of Kupres. Oh, no, no. To the west. Well, yes, that's the area of responsibility of the 2nd Army, including the Knin Corps. At that time, there were no boundaries established within the seceded state.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: We had our own regimen and --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: -- our own aspect of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, but I'm actually going to try to be quite efficient with you and if you could please listen to my questions. In paragraph 7 of your statement, you referred to events in the Kupres-Suijca area. Is it correct that the JNA 9th Corps undertook offensive activities along this axis in early April 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And just -- we'll look at this and then quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution have P4259 for the witness. Coming up will be a 9 April 1992 JNA 9th Corps regular combat report from General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the middle of item 2 is where I'm going to focus your attention. General Mladic refers to a special emphasis on the 11th Border Detachment and on planning the execution of offensive activities along the axis of Kupres-Suijca. Based on the answers you just gave, is it correct that this is the axis that you were discussing in your statement?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: I'm reading what you just cited.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, it's about middle of the way and under item 2. Approximately the middle of the page for you.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: I see soldiers have been received, cease-fire, emphasis. I don't see the axis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It should be the bullet point before what you have read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Bullet point number 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe I'm looking at a different document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I don't know if we are zoomed in too far. I believe that on the right side of the document, the Kupres-Suijca axis is just kind of cutting off just slightly. There. If it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see it now? It begins in the B/C/S with "pracena je situacija."

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Paragraph 2, commands and units of the 9th Corps --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: -- are mainly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm actually asking you from the fourth bullet point down under item 2. You see that?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: "The situation in the sector of Kupres was monitored with a special focus on ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, that's the axis that you're talking about in your statement; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the axis in Kupres. Suijca and further towards Livno.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we now go down to item 4, which is in -- on page 2 of the English translation, the part that I'll be referring to, it's towards the bottom of the B/C/S original.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. And it's at the very end of item 4 that I'm going to be referring you to, which is right at the bottom of the page, the last sentence in front of you. General Mladic indicates that the team for mopping up the battle-field has returned from the region of Kupres. Is it correct that areas of Kupres had already been liberated by 9 April 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of the B/C/S original.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's correct. That's the area that was given to us to liberate and it had been done by that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, under General Mladic's decisions at the top of the page before you, General Mladic states: "Receive and inform the 11th Operations Group of the situation in the region of Kupres." This is the operations group commanded by Stanko Ledic, which you referred to in your statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Colonel Letic, Stanko Letic. That's the group. At that time we were already at Kupres, before the 9th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, the goal and the purpose of the operations in Kupres were part of a broader process of creating a Serbian state in Bosnia and joining it with the Serbs in the Krajina region of Croatia; right?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: No, not right. How did you come up with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Kupres was a town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- could I --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could I please have 65 ter 31612 for the witness. In the B/C/S original, could we please have focus -- could we please focus on the box in the lower left corner of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a 4 May 1992 article from Glas entitled: "Colonel Stanko Letic in Sipovo, time for a Serbian army." In this article, Colonel Letic, your superior commander, states: "This is the process of creating a Serbian state in Serbian Bosnia. This is the time for Serbian accord. The Serbian people has no more blood for letting. For the sake of the unification of the Serbian people, we have to join up with the Knin Krajina. There is no more living in that state for the Ustashas, and we have to wipe the floor with them. All those capable of battle should go to fight against the Ustashas on the Kupres battle zone. This goes for the Muslims too. If they fight against the Ustashas, they will have all the same rights as the Serbs. If not, they will be second-rate citizens in the new state that will be created - the United Serbian States." Sir, as indicated by your superior, Colonel Letic, is it correct that Kupres was part of a process of creating a Serbian state in Bosnia and joining it with the Knin Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear of it. I would never believe it. That was certainly not our mission. Maybe if that was somebody's political decision or political will, it's totally different. That was not what the army was pursuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that your statements are contradicted by your own commander, his contemporaneous statements at the time. I'm not looking to debate it with you. But if you have anything else to say before I tender the document, I just want to make you aware that you are contradicted by Colonel Letic.

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: Can I say something about this? Because you've already asked me. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have anything additional to say that you have not said already about you being contradicted?

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: I don't know what you find questionable here. He's talking about the fight against the Ustasha movement. Not about any non-Serb people. What's wrong with that? I think it's perfectly all right. We had come there to defeat the Ustashas or paramilitary forces, not another people. Those who had committed --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RAJKO SARENAC
utterances.text: -- a serious crime against Serbs in Kupres. But you probably know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 31612 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence objects, Your Honours. From this document and the witness's answers, we don't know whether this reporter reported the statement by Stanko Letic correctly. This could also be a journalist's interpretation. And the witness knows nothing about this and none of it is consistent with his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm not sure that this actually needs a response, but -- and it -- obviously the witness has actually, in part, said that he sees nothing wrong with this. Number two, it's a newspaper article directly quoting his colonel at the time, Colonel Letic. It describes the position of the individual who was commanding the 11th Operations Group. It's relevant, and, you know, it's a newspaper article with a quotation from Colonel Letic expressing a view. We ask that it be admitted. It's being offered to contradict the witness with respect to the part he has not acknowledged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In any case, Mr. Stojanovic, it's not absolutely correct to say that the witness knows nothing about it. He agrees with it. He says there is nothing wrong with it. So it seems to be consistent with his understanding of the situation at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. The witness also said that that was not the mission of the Yugoslav Peoples' Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The way the journalist quoted Letic's words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. It does look like we don't understand each other here. The witness says it is not the mission of the Yugoslav Army to kill Muslims but certainly the Ustashas. So your objection is overruled. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31612 receives number P6926, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm about to actually go into a brand new area. I do see the time, and I think it may be more practical and more coherent to just start tomorrow fresh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Absolutely. Absolutely. Sir, we've come to the end of the day today. We can't carry on for today. We'll have to come back tomorrow morning again at 9.00 in the morning. But before you leave, I would like to warn you not to talk to anybody or communicate with anybody whatsoever about the testimony you have given so far or the testimony you still have to give in this case. Okay? And especially you may not talk even to the Defence team. See you tomorrow morning. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we adjourn, there is just one item that the Chamber would like to deal with. The Chamber has concerns about some of the recent video conference link motions filed by the Defence. Often the medical documentation annexed to these motions does not provide sufficient information about the witness's current health condition or how that condition might affect his ability to travel to The Hague. The Chamber reminds the parties that video conference link motions should be accompanied by supporting documentation, such as recent medical evaluations, that specifically address a witness's ability to travel, or a recent statement from the witness indicating the reasons why they are unable or unwilling to travel. Having said that, the Chamber stands adjourned to tomorrow, Wednesday, the 19th of November, 2014, in courtroom I, at 9.30 in the morning. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 19th day of November, 2014, at 9.30 a.m. 23 24 25
